advantages: Provides a TypeScript type guard: when it returns `true`, the input is narrowed to `Array<DataTypeOf<T>>`.
Validates every element against the requested runtime type, preventing mixed-type arrays from passing.
Fails fast: returns `false` as soon as a non-matching element is found.
Rejects non-arrays and empty arrays by design (depends on `isFilledArray`).

parameterDescriptions.type: The type to check against each element in the array.

shortDescription: Checks whether all elements in the given `array` are of the specified `type`.
typeScriptHint: Because `areOfType` is a type guard, TypeScript narrows the array inside an `if (areOfType(...)) {}` block to `Array<DataTypeOf<T>>`.
useCase: Use `areOfType` to validate unknown input (e.g., parsed JSON, API payloads, user input) before performing type-specific operations on every element of an array.
